title: Wild Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: Creamy Arborio rice with porcini and fresh mushrooms
excerpt: Arborio rice stirred slowly with dry white wine, mushroom stock, and a mixture of dried porcini and fresh mushrooms until silky and rich. Finished with butter and Parmesan.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto alla porcini is one of the great rice dishes of northern Italy, from the Lombardy and Piedmont regions where porcini mushrooms grow abundantly in autumn. The technique of making risotto (the gradual addition of hot stock to the rice, with constant stirring (was developed to coax maximum starch from the Arborio or Carnaroli grain, creating the characteristic creamy texture without any cream. Dried porcini are used in combination with fresh mushrooms: the dried porcini provide intense umami depth, while fresh mushrooms give texture. The soaking liquid from dried porcini is strained and added to the stock.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy-based pan for the risotto.

content.text: The stock must be hot throughout the cooking: cold stock shocks the rice and interrupts the starch release. Keep it at a simmer in a separate pan. Add the stock one ladle at a time, stirring after each addition until almost absorbed before adding the next. The risotto is ready when the rice is al dente with a creamy, flowing consistency: it should spread slightly when spooned onto a plate, not sit in a stiff mound. The mantecare (final stirring in of cold butter and Parmesan off the heat) gives the gloss.

items.preparation: soaked in 200 ml hot water for 20 minutes, drained (soaking water reserved and strained)
kept hot in a separate pan
40g for cooking, 40g cold for the finish

content.text: Add the strained porcini soaking liquid to the hot stock. Heat 20g of butter and the olive oil in a wide pan. Fry the fresh mushrooms over high heat for 5 to 6 minutes until coloured. Add the soaked porcini and thyme. Cook for 2 minutes. Remove and set aside.

In the same pan over medium heat, add 20g of butter. Cook the shallots for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are translucent at the edges. Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.

Add the hot stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly after each addition and waiting until each ladle is absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18 to 20 minutes. Add the mushrooms back to the pan after 15 minutes.

When the rice is al dente and the risotto is creamy, remove from the heat. Add the cold butter in pieces and the Parmesan. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. Season. Cover and rest for 2 minutes. Serve immediately.
